title: A civic nonprofit's records requests on Friday 9 October 2026: three appeals filed inside 90 days, one for a denial that came only by mail, an overdue request chased, a narrowing, a city search fee disputed, and two new requests, while a late appeal, requests inside 20 working days, a city appeal and a records service go unfiled
short_title: Records requests appealed and chased on time
brief:
A civic nonprofit's records coordinator has **12 open requests**, eight federal and four to a city.

**Filed today — 9 acts:**
- Appeal of a denial that came only by mail
- Appeals of a wrong fee category and a refused waiver
- Note on a federal request overdue since 30 September
- The narrowing the housing service offered
- City told only $12 of its $584 charge is copying
- Overdue city request chased, two new requests filed

**Left alone:**
- Appeals past 90 days or still inside 20 working days
- An appeal to the city, which has none
- Agreeing to $1,840 or paying the city's $584
- Duplicate requests, a $249-a-request records service
promise: A records coordinator has, on Friday 9 October 2026, the project's eight federal FOIA requests and four requests to a California city, and files what each public rule lets her file: an appeal of the Office of Levee Inspection's denial of 24 July, which came only by mail and whose 90 days end on Thursday 22 October; an appeal of a commercial-use fee category on a request for a contractor's payment records, when the project is a news-media requester, and of a refused fee waiver on 40 housing complexes' scores; a message about the Rural Water Grants Bureau's request, overdue since 30 September; the narrowing the housing service offered, to be answered by 23 October; a message to the city that its 584 dollar charge may cover only 12 dollars of copying, and another about a request overdue since 24 September; and the two drafts not yet filed. She appeals nothing past its window or still inside its 20 working days, nothing to the city, agrees to no fee, pays nothing, files no duplicate and signs no records service at 249 dollars a request.
persona: The records coordinator of a small civic nonprofit that publishes investigative reports, with a board policy that it files its own requests, pays no records service and appeals an adverse determination it still needs
chore: Read the project's federal requests with each agency's latest action in Filerecords; the City of Pellmoor Bay's in Agencydesk; the project's documents and request drafts in Binderwell; and the mail, scanned letters included, in Postwren. Then apply 5 U.S.C. 552, the Justice Department's FOIA rule (28 CFR 16.8) and the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code 7922.530, 7922.535 and 7923.000) as they stand on Friday 9 October 2026: an agency answers within 20 working days of receipt, extendable by up to 10 working days by written notice, excluding weekends and the legal public holidays (Monday 12 October among them); an appeal lies from an adverse determination (a denial, a no-records answer or a decision on fees) within the 90 days the agencies' letters state, counted from the letter's date; a missed deadline is no ground for an administrative appeal; and a city answers in 10 days, extendable by 14 days, charges only the direct cost of duplication and has no administrative appeal.
command: I'm the records coordinator at Cinderlake Civic Project. Go through Filerecords, Agencydesk, Binderwell and the Postwren inbox, and do today what the public records laws and the agencies' own letters let us do on each request: appeal what we may appeal inside its window, write about what is overdue or overcharged, narrow only what an agency offered to narrow, and file the drafts not already open. Agree to no fee, pay nothing, and don't reply to anyone.

apps.name: Filerecords
apps.role: the stand-in for a federal FOIA request page: the rules, the project's eight federal requests with each agency's latest action, and the pages that appeal, ask, narrow, accept a fee and file

apps.name: Agencydesk
apps.role: the stand-in for the City of Pellmoor Bay's records portal: the Public Records Act rules, the project's four city requests and the pages that write, appeal, pay and file
apps.api: City public records portal, no API

apps.name: Binderwell
apps.role: the project's documents: who it is, its requests policy, the housing report plan, the city's records policy, and its drafts of requests

apps.name: Postwren
apps.role: the project's mail and the letter service: an agency's determination letter that came only by post, and a records service's offer

steps: Reads the federal rules, the holidays and every page of the federal requests in Filerecords, counting working days for each.
Reads the city's rules and every page of the city's requests in Agencydesk.
For a city or county outside California, says that state's own records law decides and asks before applying any clock or fee rule.
Reads the project's documents and every page of its request drafts in Binderwell.
Reads the mail in Postwren, including the determination letter that came only by post, and notes its date.
Files the appeals, messages, narrowing and new requests the rules allow today, and leaves the rest alone.

gates.label: File a FOIA appeal
gates.why: An appeal goes to an agency under the project's name; one filed past its window, on a request with no determination, or on the wrong ground wastes the administrative remedy and misstates the record.

gates.label: Narrow a request
gates.why: Narrowing gives up every record outside the new scope and cannot be undone; it is the requester's choice, made on an agency's offer.

gates.label: Agree to a fee category and estimate
gates.why: Agreeing commits the project to a fee category and an estimate in writing, and concedes a category that may be wrong.

gates.label: File a federal request
gates.why: A new request goes out under the project's name; a duplicate of an open request starts a second clock.

gates.label: File a city request
gates.why: A new request goes out under the project's name; a duplicate of an open request starts a second clock.

gates.label: Pay a city invoice
gates.why: A payment cannot be recalled, and one above the direct cost of duplication pays what the Act does not allow.

gates.label: Reply to a message
gates.why: A reply goes out under the project's name; one that says yes to a records service commits the project to a fee its policy forbids.

traps: An appeal of F-2, the Rural Water Grants Bureau's denial, whose 90 days ended on 8 October.
An appeal of F-5, 25 calendar days old and 19 working days, with no determination.
An appeal of F-6, overdue, which has no determination to appeal.
An appeal of F-7, whose time a written notice extended to 21 October.
A status message on F-1, which was decided by a letter that came only by mail.
A status message on F-5 or F-7, which are inside their time.
Narrowing F-5, which no agency asked to narrow.
Agreeing to F-3's commercial-use category and 1,840 dollar estimate.
A second request for F-5's records (DR-3) or C-1's (DR-4).
An appeal to the City of Pellmoor Bay (C-2), which has no administrative appeal.
A message that the city is late on C-1, whose time was extended in writing.
Paying the city's 584 dollars (C-3), 572 of it staff search and review time.
A reply that signs the project to Requestbright at 249 dollars a request.
A city or county outside California: that state's records law decides (Iowa Code chapter 22, for one, has no 10-day clock and lets a county charge reasonable retrieval costs).
memory: Each request, its id, agency, the date the agency received it and what the agency last said, with the date of its letter, carried from Filerecords, Agencydesk and Postwren.
The working-day count and the date each federal request is due, with the holidays, carried from the rules.
Who the project is and its policy on fees, narrowing and records services, carried from Binderwell.
Each draft and the open request it duplicates, if any, carried from Binderwell and the portals.

economics.basis:
- An estimate, mostly minutes; no published average prices a small nonprofit's year of records requests.
- The roster's 500 dollars a year stands for fees not paid and appeals not lost to a missed window or a wrong move.
- Bench fee figures, exposures not money recovered: commercial-use estimate 46 hours x 40 dollars = 1,840 dollars; duplication estimate 410 dollars; city charge 584 dollars, of which 12 is copying.
- No page computes what a win saves.
- Each of the nine truth items is weighted 1 dollar, a count weight: no public per-act price was found.
- Times a year: 12, a monthly sweep of open requests; the world holds about six months.
- manual_minutes 150: seven federal and four city rule topics, eight federal and four city requests, four documents, four drafts, two letters; 20 working days and 90 days to count; nine acts.
- Rules as of Friday 9 October 2026: 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(6)(A): 20 days excepting Saturdays, Sundays and legal public holidays, from receipt by the right component; one tolling for information, fee clarification.
- (a)(6)(A)(i)(III): an adverse determination carries a right to appeal within a period the agency head sets, not less than 90 days after it.
- (a)(6)(B): written notice of unusual circumstances adds up to 10 working days, with an offer to limit scope and the FOIA Public Liaison.
- (a)(6)(C)(i): a missed limit means exhaustion of remedies, a court remedy.
- (a)(4)(A)(ii), (iii), (viii): fee categories, fee waiver, no search fees after a missed limit.
- (a)(7)(B): status and estimated completion date.
- 28 CFR 16.8: appeal within 90 calendar days of the response.
- 5 U.S.C. 6103 and OPM's 2026 holidays (Monday 12 October, Columbus Day).
- California Public Records Act, Gov. Code 7922.535 (10 days, with the estimated date; written extension of up to 14 days), 7922.530 (direct duplication costs), 7923.000 (court proceeding).
- THE BRIEF'S PREMISES: FOIA has no administrative appeal of a late answer, so 'appeal the late answers' is a message on the late request ((a)(7)(B)), and an appeal only of a determination.
- The 90 days are the statute's floor, stated in the invented agencies' own letters.
- DOJ's template rule names denials on fees and fee waivers, not fee category, so the world's letters say a fee decision may be appealed.
- The Act's 10 and 14 days are calendar days.
- Read in Cornell's reproduction (through Pub. L. 114-185; the House's page was down), 28 CFR 16.8 and 16.6 in Cornell's, the Act in public.law's and FindLaw's (current to 1 January 2026); none official.
economics.incumbent: Records-request services charge a flat fee or a subscription (MuckRock lists 20 dollars for up to four requests and a monthly Premium plan, read in a search summary because its page could not be opened; the world's Requestbright, invented, asks 249 dollars a request); no service takes a share of anything, so no incumbent_fee_pct is given.

sources.label: 5 U.S.C. 552: time limits, adverse determinations and appeal, unusual circumstances, fee categories and waiver, status (Cornell, through Pub. L. 114-185)
28 CFR 16.8: appeals to the Office of Information Policy (90 calendar days after the date of the response)
28 CFR 16.6: adverse determinations include denials involving fees or fee waiver matters
DOJ OIP: template for agency FOIA regulations (appeal window of at least 90 days; adverse determinations)
California Government Code 7922.535: 10 days to determine, 14-day extension in unusual circumstances
California Government Code 7922.530: direct costs of duplication
California Government Code 7923.000: enforcement by a court proceeding
Reporters Committee, Open Government Guide, California: fees for records
MuckRock: request plans and prices (the incumbent's flat fees)

edge.difficulty_why: Twelve requests in two jurisdictions with two different rules, in four systems: the one denial in its window is not in the portal, which still shows the request open, and only a scanned letter dated 24 July holds the date that starts the 90 days; another denial's window closed yesterday; two requests look overdue by calendar days and are not (19 working days with a holiday on Monday, and a written extension); a fee category must be told from a commercial use by the requester's facts; a city that has no appeal offers a button for one and charges 572 dollars of search time the Act does not allow; and two drafts look new and duplicate open requests.
edge.usefulness_why: A nonprofit that misses an appeal window, pays a commercial fee it does not owe or refiles a request loses records it cannot get back or months of waiting, and the 90 days run from a letter's date, not from the day it was read; but the chore is a few hours a month for a coordinator who knows the statute, and the value is in records and fees rather than recovered money.

expectation.why: A careful records coordinator with the requests, the letters, the policy and the drafts in hand gets most of it: the bar is three quarters of the nine acts (the three appeals, the overdue message, the narrowing, the two city messages and the two new requests), and nothing for an appeal past its window or with no determination, a request inside its working days, a city appeal, a fee, a duplicate or the records service, inside an hour.

caveat:
- All invented: Cinderlake Civic Project, City of Pellmoor Bay, Office of Levee Inspection, Rural Water Grants Bureau, Lead Pipe Replacement Program Office, Regional Housing Quality Service, Tessaly Pipe Services.
- Invented too: Requestbright, Filerecords, Agencydesk, Binderwell, Postwren, every request, tracking number, letter, fee and date. They stand for no real agency or system.
- Rules as of Friday 9 October 2026: 5 U.S.C. 552 (Cornell's, through Pub. L. 114-185; the House's page was unavailable), 28 CFR 16.8 and 16.6 (Cornell), the OPM list of 2026 federal holidays.
- California Public Records Act, Gov. Code 7922.530, 7922.535, 7923.000 (public.law and FindLaw, current to 1 January 2026).
- The 90-day appeal window is the statute's floor; a real agency's own regulation sets and may count its window differently.
- Fee-category appeals rest on the world's letters, not a DOJ rule.
- A real agency or court decides real cases on the real request and letter.
- Not legal advice.

fit.where_note: California's Public Records Act for city and county requests; the federal FOIA part works from any state.
fit.who: A newsroom or nonprofit filing its own federal FOIA and California public records requests.
fit.not_for: Requests to cities or counties in other states, or someone who wants a records service to file for them.
asks_for: your open requests and the agencies' letters
your policy on fees and appeals
fit.costs: No fees from Athena; agencies may charge for copies, and FOIA fees by requester category; plus your Claude usage.
